chapter: Leaving the band, Strayhorn and reflections
title: Daybreak Express and how Duke wrote his dreams
summary: Greer recalls Posey's slurs on Daybreak Express and Duke writing ideas between engagements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: He played that slur, I think, at the end of "Daybreak Express".
Yeah, he did, that was Posey.
On "Daybreak Express" you got the stuff
where you sound like those bells, you know, the jingle -- Clang ?
Clang, clang, clang, clang, yeah. Went the trolley, yeah.
Boy that must have been -- "Daybreak Express" must have been a shocker when you guys played that tune in person.
The other bands must have really --

Yeah, what's happening. Duke thrived on that. If he'd go along, we'd be sitting up playing cards or anything and he'd get an idea, he'd write it down on paper and start writing it, between different engagements. The first thing you know, the done / sprung it on you. Yeah. That's why I always say Duke wrote his dreams. Duke wrote his dreams. Oh, yeah, my boy was something. He didn't know -- I don't think Duke ever realized, really realized how great he was, you know. He didn't. Even when the papers raved, he never took that too serious, you know. Duke was very religious and he believed the Man was looking out for him. He didn't like all that glamor to go to his head.
